items.title: 90pct underage rape cases in Kelantan are consensual, says police
items.summary: KOTA BARU: About 90 per cent of rape cases involving underage girls in Kelantan are believed to stem from consensual relationships rather than forced sexual acts, police said. State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said, however, such cases were still investigated as statutory rape, regardless of whether the sexual activity was consensual. They are not necessarily cases involving forced rape.

items.title: Twenty-nine illegal immigrants fined up to RM10,000
items.summary: Of the 29, 15 were charged under Section 6(1)(c), 13 under Section 15(1)(c) and one under Regulation 39(b). The court fined the 15 RM6,000 each, in default two months' jail. The remaining 13 were fined RM10,000 each, in default three months' jail, while one was fined RM1,000, in default one month's jail.

items.title: Police arrest seven, including two teens, in Jalan Ampang knife‑point robbery investigation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Police arrested seven individuals, including two teenage girls, to assist in the investigation of a knife-point robbery case at a residential unit in Jalan Ampang last Friday. Wangsa Maju district police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said that the police arrested five men aged 22 to 38 and and two teenage girls aged 13 and 19 in the parking area in Jalan Metro Pudu here at 3 am yesterday. Members of the public who have information related to the incident are requested to contact the District Control Centre of the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters at 03-9289 9222, the Kuala Lumpur police Hotline at 03-2115 9999 or any nearby police station.

items.title: RXZ gatherings: Dr Dzul urges convoy organisers to strengthen rider safety measures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Organisers of mega motorcycle gatherings have a moral responsibility to ensure the safety of every participant, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. Expressing concern over accident cases involving participants of the recent RXZ Members 8.0 gathering, including fatal crashes, as well as recurring fatalities reported in previous editions of the event, Dzulkefly said such incidents were "deeply worrying". Citing the Malaysia Road Fatality Index by the Transport Ministry, Dzulkefly said an average of 18 people were killed daily in road accidents nationwide, with motorcyclists accounting for 59 per cent of fatalities.

items.title: Natural gas tariff adjustment to raise Hartalega costs, ASP gains seen limited
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The impending natural gas tariff adjustment from October 2026 is expected to increase production costs for Hartalega Holdings Bhd, although discussions on passing the higher costs to customers are still ongoing. Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) said on the export front, the current 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian glove exports to the US remains unchanged, providing some stability for local glove makers. The research firm said Hartalega could see another round of average selling price (ASP) increases amid renewed Middle East tensions.

items.title: BDO: Look beyond financial models as Malaysia's deal activity accelerates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian companies are scaling up investments in infrastructure, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), but boards risk paying a premium for assets if they focus too heavily on financial projections without adequately evaluating operational realities, an advisory firm said. BDO Malaysia executive director of advisory Fang Li Wei said the surge in investments across digital infrastructure, logistics hubs and clean energy facilities is fuelling demand for acquisitions of newly operational assets as companies look to accelerate growth and expand scale. "This gap represents the high-risk mismatch where an asset is physically operational yet fundamentally struggles to meet its business plan or meet the volume projections promised in the initial investment case," Fang said.

items.title: Hap Seng Plantations favoured on yield, growth potential
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hap Seng Plantations Bhd remains a preferred pick among Malaysian plantation stocks, supported by strong fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production growth, attractive dividend yields and an undemanding valuation. CGS International expects FY26 earnings to be supported by sector-leading FFB production growth and higher year-on-year crude palm oil (CPO) prices. The research firm is projecting a more conservative FY26 production growth of 13 per cent.

items.title: Kelantan police welcome Thai plan for 99km border fence
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan police have welcomed Thailand's plan to build a 99km barbed-wire fence along its southern border with Malaysia. State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the move could help curb cross-border crime, smuggling and the movement of unwanted elements. He said the proposed fence would complement Malaysia's efforts to strengthen security along the border and help prevent illegal cross-border movement.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls outcome proves BN does not play racial politics, says Umno veep
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The Negri Sembilan election outcome showed that voters prioritised administrative stability over racial sentiments, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. "It is untrue (that BN used racial rhetoric). Meanwhile, Wan Rosdy, who is also Pahang Menteri Besar, said the BN-PN cooperation had, for now, ended after the Negri Sembilan state election and that any future cooperation would be considered on a case-by-case basis.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning issued for 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected areas are Perlis; Kedah involving Padang Terap, Kuala Muda, Sik, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu; and Perak covering Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim The warning also covers Kelantan (Pasir Mas, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang), the whole of Terengganu, and several areas in Pahang, namely Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin. In Selangor, only Hulu Selangor is affected, while in Johor, the areas involved are Batu Pahat, Kluang, Mersing, Pontian, Kulai, Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru. For Sarawak, the affected areas include Kuching (Bau and Kuching), Betong (Saratok and Kabong), Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu, Miri (Subis, Beluru, Miri and Marudi), and Limbang.

items.title: China's central bank pledges timely policy tool adjustment
items.summary: BEIJING: China's central bank pledged to adjust monetary policy tools in a timely manner and facilitate panda bond issuance, a statement showed on Sunday. The People's Bank of China (PBOC) will continue to implement an appropriately loose monetary policy and maintain ample liquidity, according to the readout of a work meeting on Saturday to map out the second half of the year. The PBOC said it would "steadily promote the high-level opening of the financial market… advance domestic and international infrastructure cooperation, and enrich liquidity management and risk hedging tools."

items.title: Broken urinals, stagnant water raise concerns over hospital toilet conditions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Several public toilet facilities at a hospital here were found to be in unsatisfactory condition, with some male restrooms experiencing maintenance issues including broken urinals, wet floors and stagnant water. The checks found the facilities to be in a mediocre condition, with several aspects of hygiene and maintenance requiring attention. The floors were wet, toilet bowls had standing water, while several fixtures appeared to require repairs.

items.title: Thousands evacuated as Washington wildfires worsen
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A fast-moving wildfire neared the US city of Spokane on Saturday, forcing thousands of residents to evacuate as Washington state declared an emergency over one of its worst fire seasons on record. More than 200,000 acres were burning across the northwestern state during a record fourth consecutive year of statewide drought. Authorities issued the highest-level evacuation alert, "Go Now", for swathes of northern Spokane affecting thousands of people within city limits, according to the government's evacuation map.

items.title: Perhilitan relocates elephant troubling Gua Musang village
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) today successfully relocated a male elephant that frequently encroached into orchards and residential areas in Kampung Pulau Setelu here. Kelantan Perhilitan director Wan Mohd Adib Wan Yusoh said the tusked male elephant is estimated to be between 15 and 18 years old. He said the operation involved 19 personnel, including team members from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Sungai Deka, Terengganu, and Kuala Gandah, Pahang.

items.title: Shooter among three dead in Idaho shopping centre attack
items.summary: BOISE: Three people died after a gunman opened fire in a shopping area in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, according to a city spokesman. Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks told reporters the shooter was dead and the threat to the community was over. The shooter was among the dead, Hicks said.

items.title: WestJet flight attendants go on strike after talks fall through, grounding flights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Flight attendants at Canada's WestJet went on strike on Sunday after failing to reach a deal with the country's second-largest carrier, grounding flights during the busy summer travel season. The strike follows a four-day work stoppage by flight attendants last August at larger rival Air Canada, highlighting broader efforts by flight attendants in Canada and the US to challenge a compensation structure that mostly pays cabin crew when an aircraft is in motion. CUPE on Sunday said it had tried until the last minute to reach a deal but that "WestJet's offer did not go far enough."

items.title: China flash flood death toll rises to 25
items.summary: BEIJING: The toll from a flash flood in northwest China has risen to 25 dead, with 23 injured, state media reported Sunday a week after the disaster. The flood ripped through the Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a tourist spot popular with day campers, on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injured. The updated toll came as the country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event, Xinhua said.

items.title: HBA: Build-then-sell could break Malaysia's abandoned housing crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's long-debated Build-Then-Sell (BTS) model could offer a solution to the country's persistent abandoned housing crisis, but developers have remained reluctant to adopt a system that would require them to bear greater upfront financial risks. As of June 30, Malaysia had 303 private housing projects classified as "sick" projects, involving 43,288 housing units with a gross development value (GDV) of RM40.25 billion. The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), in a written reply published on the Parliament website, said 100 projects had been confirmed as abandoned, affecting 27,998 housing units and 14,961 buyers.

items.title: 13-year-old girl among seven arrested over knifepoint robbery
items.summary: Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the case came to light after the victim lodged a police report at 9.02pm on July 31. "Following investigations, a team from the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters arrested five men aged between 22 and 38, and two females aged 13 and 19, at a parking area in Jalan Metro Pudu about 3am on Aug 1," he said in a statement. Police urged those with information on the case to contact the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters control centre at 03-9289 9222, the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or the nearest police station.

items.title: Kelantan lockups not overcrowded despite drug arrest directive
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan police have assured that state lockups are not overcrowded despite a recent directive requiring every station chief to arrest at least one drug addict daily. State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said concerns over lockup capacity should not hinder efforts to tackle the state's drug problem. Yusoff was responding to reports that he had instructed all station chiefs to detain at least one drug addict daily as part of efforts to curb criminal activities and drug abuse statewide.

items.title: RTD: No compromise on offences at RXZ Members gatherings
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) will step up enforcement against motorcycle gathering programmes, including RXZ Members, while holding engagement sessions with organisers amid recurring accidents linked to such events. RTD director‑general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department does not prohibit motoring programmes, but participants must comply with traffic laws and vehicle technical regulations. Aedy Fadly stressed RTD will not compromise against participants who endanger other road users, noting public complaints about traffic congestion and reckless riding.

items.title: BN morale soars after toppling PH heavyweights in Negri Sembilan polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's victory in two closely watched Negri Sembilan seats, Chennah and Linggi, has boosted the coalition's morale after it successfully defeated two high-profile Pakatan Harapan figures. The defeats of DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke in Chennah and former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun in Linggi emerged as among the biggest surprises of the state election, with both seats attracting intense attention from political observers, party machinery and voters throughout the campaign. Chennah had long been regarded as a DAP stronghold , with Loke holding the seat since 2013.

items.title: Negri Sembilan DAP backs Loke to remain state chairman
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan DAP has thrown its full support behind Anthony Loke to remain the party's state chairman, despite his offer to step down after failing to retain the Chennah state seat in the state election. State DAP secretary Cha Kee Chin said the state committee had unanimously agreed that Loke should continue leading the party. Cha said Negri Sembilan DAP requires Loke's experienced leadership to face future challenges, including the 16th General Election (GE16).

items.title: Saudi crown prince, Trump hold call on Middle East tensions
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman and US President Donald Trump held a call aimed at reducing regional tensions, the kingdom's official SPA press agency reported Sunday. "His Royal Highness emphasised the necessity of prioritising dialogue to reduce tensions and the importance of exerting all possible efforts to achieve a truce that paves the way for diplomatic solutions," SPA reported after Trump said he had decided to hold off on renewed attacks on Iran after requests from Gulf countries.--AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Lee Lam Thye calls for urgent animal management reforms after dog's death in Klang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Local authorities and state ministries must immediately implement critical reforms to animal management protocols to prevent further cases of animal cruelty, says animal welfare advocate Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye. He said key measures must include adopting the Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release/Return (TNVR) approach, standardising humane capture techniques, strictly prohibiting private property seizures, and establishing independent oversight committees. "Local councils must formally mandate TNVR policies, partnering directly with recognised animal welfare NGOs and local veterinary networks to manage stray populations humanely," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Pilot held in Indonesia over ecstasy pills smuggling had no prior record
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Indonesia recently for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills had no prior criminal or drug-related record in Malaysia, police said. Bukit Aman Narcotic Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed this when contacted today. Hussein said investigations into the case, including cooperation with the Indonesian authorities, were ongoing.

items.title: Fire breaks out at Sunway Square Mall, blaze contained before firefighters arrive (VIDEO)
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 2 — A small kitchen fire at a restaurant in Sunway Square Mall was extinguished even before firefighters reached the scene early this morning, according to the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department. According to the New Straits Times , the department received an emergency call at 1.23am and dispatched a team from the Subang Jaya station. Eight personnel, a fire engine and a water tanker were deployed.

items.title: Negri Sembilan exco lineup expected by Friday, says MB
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: The lineup of the Negeri Sembilan state executive council is expected to be finalised by this Friday at the latest, said newly appointed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. He said discussions with the Barisan Nasional leadership would be held first before the proposed lineup is presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, for approval. Ismail said he would also meet Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi soon to seek his views on the composition of the state executive council, including the possibility of appointing state elected representatives from Perikatan Nasional.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB: New state government committed to upholding royal institution
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today pledged that the state government would continue to uphold the royal institution and preserve the state’s customs and traditions as fundamental pillars of its administration. He said safeguarding the royal institution was the responsibility of every Negeri Sembilan citizen and remained essential to maintaining harmony and close relations between the monarchy and the state administration. Meanwhile, Ismail said the state government would continue strengthening cooperation with the Federal Government to ensure the interests and well-being of the people of Negeri Sembilan remained a priority.

items.title: Melaka polls could be held at any time, Rauf hints
items.summary: MELAKA: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the Melaka state election could be held at any time following Barisan Nasional's victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan. He said the current Melaka state assembly's term expires on Dec 31. Before this, he said the outcome of the Johor and Negri Sembilan polls would be taken into account in seeking the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly.

items.title: Open to negotiations: Melaka MB says willing to discuss cooperation with any party for the coming state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 2 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) is open to cooperating with any party under a BN Plus formula for the upcoming state election, its chairman and Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno liaison committee chairman, said the party welcomed discussions with any political party interested in working together for the state polls. The election saw BN win 18 state seats, PH 11 and PN seven, enabling BN and PN to form the Negeri Sembilan state government.

items.title: OPEC+ has agreement in principle for September quota increase and pause thereafter, source says
items.summary: LONDON: OPEC+ plans to approve a production quota increase on Sunday of around 188,000 barrels per day (bpd) from September, after which it will pause further output increases, sources said, as the group completes the unwinding of voluntary cuts. The seven core members of OPEC+ — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — have been increasing monthly production quotas for most of this year. After September, the group will likely pause output increases for the rest of the year, one OPEC+ delegate and one OPEC+ source said, as the alliance faces potentially difficult talks over new production quotas.

items.title: Vietnam's energy-saving drive gathers pace amid soaring summer power demand
items.summary: HANOI: Businesses and households across Vietnam are stepping up electricity-saving measures and investing in rooftop solar power as prolonged heatwaves push electricity demand to record levels, Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported. 10/CT-TTg on electricity saving and rooftop solar development. This helps reduce electricity costs while ensuring sufficient power is available for other services," Tuan said.

items.title: Tawau Port acquires two new dock cranes worth RM70mil
items.summary: TAWAU: The acquisition of two new quay cranes worth RM70 million for Tawau Port is expected to boost port efficiency and strengthen its role as a key maritime gateway on Sabah's east coast. Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the investment is a strategic step to strengthen the state's port infrastructure and support Sabah's long-term economic growth. He noted that the investment also reflects the state government's commitment through Sabah Ports Sdn Bhd (SPSB) to modernise critical infrastructure, enhancing efficiency and competitiveness of Sabah's ports, particularly on the state's east coast.

items.title: Discussions with PN in Melaka won't necessarily result in pact, says BN's Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA: The winning momentum from Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional's understanding in Negri Sembilan will lead to a "BN Plus" arrangement in Melaka, although discussions with PN may not necessarily result in a political pact. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said the "BN Plus" formula reflected the state chapter's openness to negotiations with any party. However, he said all decisions would ultimately align with BN's interests and strength in the state.

items.title: Gesture of appreciation: Negeri Sembilan MB announces special state public holiday tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Newly sworn-in Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today announced a special public holiday for the state tomorrow, saying it is meant to recognise the efforts of those involved in the recently concluded state election. Speaking at his first press conference after taking his oath of office, Ismail said the holiday had received the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. “His Royal Highness has also graciously consented for me to announce a special public holiday tomorrow for the people of Negeri Sembilan,” he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan exco lineup to be discussed with Zahid, finalised by Friday, says new MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Newly sworn-in Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today that the composition of the state executive council (exco) will be discussed with Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi before a final decision is made, with appointments expected by Friday. Speaking to reporters after taking his oath of office, Ismail said he would also seek the views of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan before the lineup is finalised. Mohd Zuhaimi and Mohd Aidil secured 506 votes and 2,816 votes, respectively.

items.title: Police probe viral Pandamaran car park brawl involving 16-year-old student
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 2 — Police are investigating a viral video on social media showing a brawl at the Pandamaran Sports Complex car park in Klang last Friday. Klang Selatan police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the incident occurred at approximately 1.20pm involving two men, one of whom is a 16-year-old student. Lim urged anyone with information on the incident to come forward and contact the investigating officer, Insp Mohammad Baaz Mohd Zohari, at 016-4117885, the Klang Selatan IPD operations room at 03-3376 2222, or any nearby police station.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz tells Negeri Sembilan assemblymen to put people above politics
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, today reminded members of the State Legislative Assembly to always place the interests of the state and its people above political or personal considerations in carrying out the mandate entrusted to them. His Royal Highness said every elected representative bears a significant responsibility, as they are entrusted with bringing the voices, aspirations, needs, and concerns of the people to the State Legislative Assembly. Tuanku Muhriz stressed that every policy, plan, and decision made should reflect those aspirations and remain firmly focused on the welfare of the people and the continued development of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: BN will deliver responsible and people-centred govt in Negeri Sembilan, says Zambry
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate entrusted to the coalition by voters in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election would be translated into a responsible, people-centred administration anchored on stability, integrity, and the state’s continued development. Zambry also thanked party members, campaign workers, election machinery, volunteers, and supporters whose dedication contributed to BN’s performance in the state election. The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on June 5 after the state BN withdrew its support for the leadership of Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun on April 27, triggering the state election For the latest news on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Who is Ismail Lasim, the new Negeri Sembilan menteri besar?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Datuk Ismail Lasim has been officially sworn in as the new menteri besar of Negeri Sembilan before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. The ceremony marks a major transition in the state’s leadership, elevating a veteran politician and legal practitioner to the top executive office after more than two decades of public service in state administration. Ismail’s rise to the state’s highest political office comes as a continuation of his long-standing presence in Negeri Sembilan politics.

items.title: It’s official: Ismail Lasim takes over as Negeri Sembilan menteri besar
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Juasseh State Assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim was today sworn in as the new Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan. Barisan Nasional (BN) deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and other state elected representatives were also present. In the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election, PH won 17 state seats, followed by BN (14) and PN (five), leading to the formation of a PH-BN state government.

items.title: Ismail Lasim among three tipped for Negeri Sembilan menteri besar post
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Kuala Pilah Umno chief Datuk Ismail Lasim is among three candidates tipped to be appointed as Negeri Sembilan’s new Menteri Besar. Ismail, 67, who is also a member of the Umno Supreme Council, won the Juasseh state seat in yesterday’s 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. The two other names being floated are Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, 62, the Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison chairman and Jelebu MP who retained the Pertang state seat, and Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, 47, the former state deputy speaker who won the Lenggeng seat.

items.title: Selangor Veterinary Department probes viral dog abuse incident in Port Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 2 — The Selangor Department of Veterinary Services (JPV Selangor) has launched a criminal investigation after a video showing a group of individuals restraining and dragging a dog by its neck went viral, culminating in the animal’s death. According to the department, multiple complaints were lodged through the MyAnimalWelfare system at around 9.25pm on 30 July 2026 after the video began circulating online. On 31 July, at about 11am, JPV Selangor’s Animal Welfare Team received the carcass of a male dog — believed to be the same animal seen in the video — along with an orange icebox from a local woman who surrendered the remains.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan to swear In new menteri besar this morning, chosen candidate still unknown
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan will install its new menteri besar this morning, with the swearing‑in ceremony scheduled to take place at the Balairung Seri, Istana Besar Seri Menanti at 10.15am, according to a media notice shared via WhatsApp. Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he submitted three names to the Yang di‑Pertuan Besar during an audience at Istana Hinggap last night, stressing that the choice rests entirely with the ruler. The swearing‑in follows the outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, where BN won 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured 11, and Perikatan Nasional (PN) took seven.

items.title: Man drowns after saving eight-year-old great-nephew from Terengganu river
items.summary: Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said firefighters recovered the body of Harun Ibrahim from the riverbank at about 7.30 pm, about 100 metres from the spot where he was reported missing. “The victim was eventually found on the riverbank by the Malaysia Fire and Rescue Department’s Water Rescue Team after the water level dropped during the search and rescue operation. Police advise the public to remain vigilant and exercise caution when visiting water recreation areas, given the recent spell of unpredictable weather,” he said.

items.title: After viral video shows young girl being molested, Sungai Buloh police searching for perpetrator
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Police are tracking down a foreign man suspected of molesting an 11-year-old girl at a business premises in Sungai Buloh, Selangor, on Wednesday (July 29). Sungai Buloh police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said they received a report from the Kampung Baru Subang police station regarding the incident. He urged those with information regarding the case to contact the investigation officer, Insp Muhammad Amirul Amin Shukor, at 013-6695290 or the nearest police station.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan state election sees 30 candidates losing their deposits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — A total of 30 candidates lost their deposits after failing to garner at least one-eighth of the total of votes counted in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), which did not win a single seat and failed to defend its Labu seat, suffered the biggest loss, with 23 out of 24 of its candidates losing their deposits. Also, the sole candidate from Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (ASLI) and Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) both lost their deposit, along with one Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate, and four independent candidates.

items.title: Out of nine women candidates in Negeri Sembilan polls, only three winners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Only three of nine women candidates who contested in the Negeri Sembilan state election prevailed over their opponents, according to the Election Commission’s (EC) official results. S Leza (6,830 votes) won by a majority of 730 votes against PH candidate Datuk Noorzunita Begum (6,100 votes), while Siti Nur Umaira (14,209 votes) won by a majority of 5,279 votes against PH candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu’s Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes). Meanwhile, Nicole Tan defended her Bukit Kepayang seat with a majority of 15,207 votes by polling 24,096 votes against PN’s Lee Boon Shian, who garnered 8,889 votes.

items.title: Both youngest and oldest winning Negeri Sembilan state election winners from Umno
items.summary: Siti Nur Umaira, the Rasah Umno Puteri division chief, secured 14,209 votes to win the seat with a majority of 5,279 votes, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu incumbent Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes). Meanwhile, Mohamad retained the Rantau state seat by securing 19,050 votes to defeat PH’s Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi (7,032 votes) in a straight fight. He polled 32,004 votes in a three-cornered fight, defeating PH’s Ahmad Shahir Mohd Shah (15,045 votes) and Bersatu’s Mohd Nazree Mohd Yunus (2,205 votes).

items.title: Selangor to review stray animal management SOPs across all local authorities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 2 — The Selangor state government will review the standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing stray animals across all local authorities to ensure enforcement operations are carried out more effectively, safely and humanely. “The state government remains committed to safeguarding public safety, while at the same time enhancing animal welfare practices and upholding public trust in the integrity and professionalism of government agencies,” he said in a statement yesterday. Ng said the state government also expressed its appreciation for the advice of Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who emphasised the importance of compassion towards animals and the principle that no one is above the law.

items.title: Pakatan leaders vow collective responsibility for Negeri Sembilan loss, pledge continued commitment to constituents
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — All Pakatan Harapan (PH) leaders will take collective responsibility for the coalition’s defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said last night. He said the coalition’s leadership, from the highest level down to the grassroots, would shoulder responsibility collectively, stressing that no individual, group, community or faction would be singled out for blame. According to unofficial results, PH has garnered 11 of 36 seats it contested in the election, while Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured 18 and seven seats respectively.

items.title: Zahid: BN submits three names for Negeri Sembilan menteri besar post
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said that the coalition has submitted three names of candidates for the position of Menteri Besar to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. The Umno president said he delivered the official letter during an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap here tonight. Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz granted an audience to Ahmad Zahid at approximately 10 pm.

items.title: PM Anwar pledges continued cooperation, federal support for Negeri Sembilan government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the federal government will continue to extend its support and cooperation to the new Negeri Sembilan state government for the well-being and prosperity of the state and its people. Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) would form the Negeri Sembilan state government after securing a two-thirds majority win in the state polls. The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly has 36 seats.

items.title: Seismic shift in Malaysian politics as BN-Perikatan ousts Pakatan heavyweights in Negeri Sembilan poll
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan woke up to a transformed political landscape this morning after voters decisively handed control of the state to a Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) alliance. The outcome effectively toppled the Pakatan Harapan (PH) administration and unseated two of the coalition’s most powerful figures: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun. Unofficial data from the Election Commission (EC) indicated that BN emerged as the largest bloc with 18 seats, while PN took seven.

items.title: Pakatan blames ‘racial politics’ after defeat to BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has attributed its dismal performance in today’s Negeri Sembilan state election to "racial and identity politics," cautioning that such polarising tactics threaten to fracture the state’s multi-ethnic social fabric. The coalition’s Election Department confirmed that PH unofficially won in only 11 of the 36 seats contested. “This state election witnessed an extraordinary campaign of racial politics based almost entirely on identity, which has the potential to sow division within society and the state.

items.title: Zahid: BN and Perikatan will partner to establish Negeri Sembilan administration
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will form the new Negeri Sembilan government after securing a two-thirds majority in today’s state election, based on unofficial results. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the unofficial results showed BN had won 18 seats while PN secured seven, giving the two coalitions a combined majority to form the state administration. Ahmad Zahid said the new state government will be built on an understanding between BN and PN, while upholding the mandate given by the people.

items.title: A ride cut short: Homeward-bound varsity student dies on highway after RXZ 8.0 gathering in Gong Badak
items.summary: DUNGUN, Aug 1 — A private university student was killed when the motorcycle he was riding skidded at Kilometre 354 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near here, today. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said 22-year-old Muhammad Bakhtiar Mazlan, from Parit Raja, Batu Pahat, Johor, was confirmed dead at the scene due to severe head injuries. He said police received a call from members of the public regarding the incident involving a Honda Vario motorcycle at about 3pm.

items.title: Economy Ministry eyes pilot project as Malaysia’s ageing population threatens fiscal and care pressures
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 1 — The Economy Ministry is identifying a pilot project to address challenges arising from Malaysia’s ageing population, with plans to roll it out next year. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the ageing agenda had been designated as a key pillar under the 13th Malaysia Plan. He said planning for the second rolling plan for next year’s development expenditure would be structured to cover all segments, including initiatives to address population ageing.

items.title: Myvi and Saga collide near Kelantan school, 80-year-old woman dies, four others seriously injured
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 1 — An 80-year-old woman was killed while four others, including two drivers, were seriously injured in a two-car collision near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Kedai Piah, Ketereh, here this afternoon. Ketereh Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Nazri Taib said firefighters arrived at the scene four minutes after receiving an emergency call at 3.25pm. “Four other victims aged between nine and 38, including both drivers, suffered serious injuries,” he said in a statement today.
